title: Operational Skyline: SLO Rollout Sprint Catalog & Rotational Runway
body:
Purpose and high-level idea:
This doc catalogs a repeatable sprint structure and rotational runway for cross-functional SLO work. Goal is to make reliability upgrades and SLO adoption predictable across product teams while limiting context-switch load on SREs. Think of the program as a seasonal catalogue of 2-week sprints with a lightweight, repeatable checklist that product teams can opt into.

Objectives (measurable):
- Baseline adoption: onboard 6 feature teams to the SLO lifecycle process by end of Q2 2026.
- Visibility: surface per-route latency + error SLI within 24 hours for new adopters.
- Risk control: ensure every canary has automated rollback criteria and a documented fallback policy.

Scope:
- Included: model-serving endpoints, hosted-api routes, dedicated capacity ingress.
- Excluded: embeddings-only batch jobs, third-party integrations (unless they affect token reliability).

Key stakeholders and role sketch:
- SRE Program Lead (Maya Chen) — cadence owner, sprint facilitation, escalation triage.
- Product Reliability Liaisons (one per product squad) — coordinate squad readiness, run experiment.
- Infra Engineering (Ethan P.) — SLO metric ingestion and alert plumbing.
- Observability (Lea T.) — dashboard templates, instrumentation QA.
- Solutions/SE (Ravi S.) — customer-impact assessment and mitigation play.
- Oncall rotation (Nora L.) — on-call availability during rollout week.

Sprint catalog (2-week pattern templates):
1) Discover & Baseline (wk1): data capture shadow, ask: what are realistic traffic percentiles? Deliverable: baseline SLI report + target proposal.
2) Instrument & Guard (wk2): add missing 95/99p latency telemetry, define error classifications, wire alerts to dev channels. Deliverable: instrumentation PR and alert runbook.
3) Canary & Measure (wk3): run controlled canary, measure degradation, collect customer-impact signals. Deliverable: canary dashboard + rollback triggers.
4) Harden & Automate (wk4): implement automated fallback and incident play; add SLO dashboard to team home. Deliverable: automated fallback + postmortem template.

Rotational runway (how teams sign up):
- Quarterly intake window (first two weeks of quarter) for new teams.
- Rolling smaller cohorts monthly for urgent/high-ROI teams.
- Each intake gets a 4-sprint pathway (8 weeks) from baseline to hardened automation.

Governance and decision rules:
- SLO approval committee (SRE lead + 2 product liaisons) signs off on targets.
- Any target that increases error budget consumption > 15% requires Exec notification.
- Fast-fail policy: if canary breaches rollback thresholds 2x in 24h -> immediate rollback and incident review.

Communications & rituals:
- Weekly sync: 30m standing with squad liaisons during active sprints.
- Sprint kickoff doc: template with scope, SLIs, owners, acceptance criteria.
- Mid-sprint gladiator demo: short live run of canary dashboards to SRE + product PMs.
- Post-sprint retro + follow-ups in #reliability-program channel.

Acceptance checklist (must be all true to graduate):
- SLIs instrumented and surfaced in central dashboard.
- Alerts firing in dev channel with runbook links.
- Canary executed with < defined rollback violation.
- Incident playbook created and linked in ticket.
- SLO target reviewed and committee-approved.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: teams under-estimate noise in 99p metrics -> Mitigation: ensure min 72h steady-state shadow before canary.
- Risk: alert fatigue -> Mitigation: temporary suppression windows and increased alert thresholds during data-collection phase.
- Risk: resource contention for infra changes -> Mitigation: slot infra work into a separate "infra week" cadence and reserve capacity.

Operational metrics to track program health:
- Time to onboard (days from signup to first canary).
- % of teams with dashboards in 14 days.
- Number of canary-triggered rollbacks per month.
- Change in customer-visible error budget burn for participating services.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Explore lightweight templating to generate SLI dashboards automatically from an API.
- Should we create a lightweight "SLO coach" role (0.2 FTE) per quarter? cost/impact tradeoff analysis needed.
- Need legal check for private deployments where telemetry may be restricted.

Next immediate actions (first two weeks):
- Finalize intake form and publish to product liaisons (Owner: Maya Chen, by 2026-01-21).
- Create baseline SLI report template (Owner: Lea Thompson, by 2026-01-22).
- Book first cohort: invite 3 product teams to pilot (Owner: Ravi Singh, by 2026-01-28).

Appendix: useful links and templates:
- SLI reporting template: confluence:REL-Runway-2026
- SLO signoff checklist: github:infra/slo-templates#58
- Intake form draft: doc:shared_drives/engineering/sre/slo-intake-draft

---
Notes: This is intentionally pragmatic and iterative. The catalog is meant to be updated after each cohort with concrete time-to-value and retro actions. Keep backlog items lightweight and prioritize automation that reduces human toil on repeated sprints.
